title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to test whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves operational oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The null result is design‑bound: every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle and thus the repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑grounded recommendations (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests) for informative follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are being investigated as intent→configuration agents for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness must be enforced because plausible outputs can be unsafe or semantically incorrect for live devices. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: a generator proposes a candidate configuration; a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties (reachability, protected resources, transient‑state invariants); and, if validation fails, a repair module produces a corrected candidate. Prior work (constraint‑guided generation, verifier‑grounded repair, intent‑to‑config benchmarks) reports improvements from verifier integration, but published comparisons often lack preregistration, exhaustive artifact archives, or auditor‑grade traceability. Our study uses a fully preregistered, autonomously executed, artifact‑hashed workflow to produce an auditable confirmatory measurement of whether verifier assistance increases oracle pass rates under a precisely specified design.

The preregistration froze the key design levers: the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), repair budget (≤1 call/task), and the paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Those frozen choices are archived and hashed per the manifest (see provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba and preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). The central methodological consequence of the shared_initial_candidate semantics is that a single generated candidate per pair was supplied to both the baseline and the guarded condition; thus repairs could only act if the single shared candidate failed the validator.
sections.related_work: Recent NetOps research has explored intent translation, constraint‑augmented generation, verifier‑assisted repair, and NetOps benchmarking. Representative artifact‑verified works include constraint‑guided agents that improve accuracy by encoding domain invariants (MeshAgent, 2025), intent→configuration benchmarks (NetConfEval, 2024), and verifier‑grounded repair systems in other DSLs (StruSpec style artifacts). Those studies motivated our preregistration and informed validator design choices; however, they typically evaluated systems under independent sampling regimes or with iterative repair budgets larger than one. Our run differs by (a) preregistering generation semantics and the estimand, (b) archiving end‑to‑end provider traces and validator traces with SHA‑256 digests, and (c) executing the full paired analysis pipeline autonomously and reproducibly. The supplied evidence bundle contains the nearest artifacts used for literature grounding (cited_record_ids included).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental plan: study‑cnd‑2026‑001 froze the scientific design before execution. Key preregistered elements (artifact hashes in execution manifest) were: model = gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, paired Npairs = 200, and analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (paired bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729).

Task bank, stratification, and manifest: The confirmatory task bank comprised 200 paired tasks stratified by protocol: BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each. Vendor allocation per protocol followed the preregistration (Cisco 17 / Juniper 17 / Arista 16 per protocol; totals Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64) and complexity was evenly split (100 simple / 100 complex). Each task manifest entry contains an intent, initial and expected final states, required_sequence constraints, and a reference_answer; representative items are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl and example scoring artifacts at execution/scoring/*.json (see execution_manifest SHA‑256 listings).

Generation, adapter, validator and scoring semantics: The frozen adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 mediated calls to the declared LLM (gpt‑5‑mini). The shared_initial_candidate policy consumed one generator call per pair and supplied the identical generated candidate to both paired conditions. The deterministic validator parsed and semantically simulated the proposed candidate against the emulated network model to produce normalized_configuration, validity boolean, parsed_command_count, and a validator trace. All scoring outputs and validator traces were archived (execution/scoring/*.json) and hashed. Repair was permitted by the preregistration but, in the executed run, repair was never invoked (repair_applied=false in all validator traces). The complete execution manifest lists all raw responses, provider traces, and per‑file SHA‑256 digests to support deterministic reconciliation.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑backed): The autonomous run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). All raw responses, provider traces, and scoring JSON files are archived under execution/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (representative digests: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 f51ee54d..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce925...; see manifest).

Confirmatory outcomes (artifact numbers): The deterministic validator accepted the shared candidate for every pair. Summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...) show baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. The paired estimate of paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline is 0.00; the paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI is [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. All analysis artifacts and logs are archived (analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...). Representative per‑task scoring JSONs (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) include normalized_configuration, validator final_state, parsed_command_count, validity=true and repair_applied=false.

Interpretation: The preregistered estimand under the frozen shared_initial_candidate semantics is well‑defined and answered by these results. However, because every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the repair stage was never exercised and therefore no opportunity existed for guarded repair to improve outcomes. The observed null effect is therefore a direct consequence of the preregistered generation semantics and the specific model‑task interaction of this run, not a general refutation of verifier‑assisted architectures.
sections.discussion:
Design‑bound null result and ceiling effect: The shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generated candidate per pair consumed by both conditions) reduced the model call budget (model_calls_used=200) but created a deterministic ceiling: if the single shared candidate passes the oracle, guarded repairs cannot act. The execution artifacts document that behavior: repair_calls_invoked=0; every validator trace includes repair_applied=false. The artifact bundle and deterministic_reconciliation.json demonstrate internal accounting consistency and make the causal chain auditable.

Operational lessons (artifact‑grounded): To evaluate verifier‑assisted repair meaningfully, experimental designs must permit the generator and repair stages to be exercised. Two immediate, artifact‑anchored follow‑ups are reproducible from the archive: (1) independent_per_condition generation semantics (one generator call per condition per pair) — this variant increases model_calls (≈400 generator calls) and allows baseline candidate failures to exist independently of guarded candidates, enabling repair invocation; (2) calibrated or adversarial task insertion — extend execution/task_manifest.jsonl with higher difficulty or boundary tasks (oracle‑coverage stress tests) so that some shared or independent baseline candidates fail the validator and trigger repair. Both variants can be executed using the same adapter and seedable task generator described in the manifest; per‑file hashing will produce new manifests for audit.

Threats to validity (artifact‑anchored): Internal validity — the primary threat was the preregistered generation semantics; we report it openly and provide SHA‑256 evidence of the frozen choice. Construct validity — the deterministic validator enforces emulation‑based oracles (reachability, protected interfaces, transient rules) but may miss real device quirks; validator coverage diagnostics are included in per‑pair scoring artifacts. External validity — single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic emulation limit generalization to other models and production images. Conclusion validity — the paired analysis is correct for the frozen estimand, but the observed null is design‑bound and does not generalize to settings where repairs are exercised.

Reproducibility and audit: Every prompt, raw LLM response, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, task manifest entry, and analysis artifact is archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...) verifies that the per‑file accounting is consistent. To rerun a variant that allows repair to act, change generation_semantics in a new preregistration and rerun the adapter; the same execution harness will archive provider calls and produce a new immutable manifest for audit.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the declared model and validator, we observed no difference between baseline and guarded conditions because the single shared generated candidate passed the deterministic oracle in every pair. The run therefore answers the specific preregistered estimand but is not informative about repair efficacy in regimes where generator variance produces validator failures. We publish the complete artifact bundle (prompts, preregistration, provider traces, raw outputs, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) so researchers can reproducibly execute follow‑ups (independent generation, higher difficulty tasks, larger repair budgets) that allow repairs to be exercised and assessed.

The preregistration froze the primary hypothesis, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, deterministic validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- LLM and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini used via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair and provided to both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json SHA‑256 f51ee54d...).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed deterministic emulation‑based validation and produced the normalized_configuration and validator traces for each episode (representative scoring file: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b).
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (repair_applied=false in every validator trace). Repair prompts and repair provider traces would have been archived if used.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples (seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4db7c...).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms arithmetic and accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...).
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs excluded; repair stage not triggered. Full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are included in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived and annotated in the artifact bundle.
